lessons.title: Regular verbs
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Mia clean the dusty attic and talk about what they did yesterday.

items.example: Mia watched TV yesterday.
items.note: Add -ed to 'watch' to talk about something you saw on a screen in the past.

items.example: My father cooked dinner last night.
items.note: Use 'cooked' when someone made hot food in the past.

items.example: We visited our grandmother last weekend.
items.note: Say 'visited' when you went to see a person or a place.

items.example: Sam helped his mother in the kitchen.
items.note: Use 'helped' when someone did work to make things easier for another person.

items.example: I cleaned my bedroom on Saturday.
items.note: Say 'cleaned' after you wash or tidy a dirty room or thing.

items.example: They walked to the park yesterday.
items.note: Use 'walked' when someone went somewhere on foot.

grammar.title: Past simple with -ed
grammar.explanation: Add -ed to regular verbs to talk about finished actions in the past. The verb stays the same for I, you, he, she, we, and they.

practice.prompt: Mia was in the living room with the TV on yesterday. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: Use watched for TV or films in the past.

practice.prompt: Listen and choose what you heard.
practice.audio: He cooked rice and chicken for dinner.
practice.answer: He cooked rice and chicken for dinner.
options: He cooked rice and chicken for dinner.
He cleaned the kitchen at night.
He walked to school with Mia.
practice.explanation: Cooked means he made the food.

practice.prompt: Smarty went to see his grandmother. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: Smarty ___ his grandmother last weekend.
practice.explanation: Use visited when you go to see family or friends.

practice.prompt: Match each past verb to the matching phrase.
practice.explanation: Each -ed verb pairs with the action it describes.

practice.prompt: Put the words in order to say what we did yesterday.
practice.explanation: Use cleaned with -ed because yesterday is in the past.

practice.prompt: Leo worked with his father in the garden. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: Leo ___ his father yesterday.
practice.explanation: Helped shows Leo gave his father support.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: I walked to the park with my friend.
practice.answer: I walked to the park with my friend.
practice.explanation: Walked is the regular past form of walk.

story.hook: Why is the old room so clean now?

image.describe: Smarty the black cat and Mia stand in a bright, tidy wooden attic holding a broom and a duster beside clean boxes.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Look at this room, Smarty! It is clean now.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Yes! We cleaned it yesterday.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: You helped me with the big box.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: And in the evening, we walked to the park.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: After the park, my mother cooked soup, and we watched TV.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: It was a good day!

questions.prompt: When did Smarty and Mia clean the room?
questions.explanation: Smarty says: We cleaned it yesterday.

questions.prompt: What did Mia's mother do after the park?
questions.explanation: Mia says: my mother cooked soup.

mission.setup: Smarty asks what you did yesterday. Answer in your own words using regular past verbs.

turns.smarty: Yesterday I cleaned my room. What did you do yesterday?
turns.hint: Start with 'I' and use a verb ending in -ed like watched, cooked, or cleaned.

turns.smarty: Nice! Did you help someone or visit someone last weekend?
turns.hint: Say 'I helped...' or 'I visited...'

lessons.title: Irregular verbs
lessons.scenario: In the attic, Sam and Smarty unpack a box and talk about what they got and made.

items.example: Sam came to my home yesterday.
items.note: Use 'came' as the past form of 'come' when someone arrived somewhere.

items.example: She took her umbrella because it was rainy.
items.note: Say 'took' as the past form of 'take' when someone carried or picked up something.

items.example: We made a big cake for my birthday.
items.note: Use 'made' as the past form of 'make' when someone built or prepared something.

items.example: I got a new book from my uncle.
items.note: Say 'got' as the past form of 'get' when you received or obtained something.

items.example: Lily gave me an apple at lunch.
items.note: Use 'gave' as the past form of 'give' when someone handed a gift or item to another person.

items.example: They bought fresh bread at the market.
items.note: Say 'bought' as the past form of 'buy' when someone paid money for something.

grammar.title: Irregular past verbs
grammar.explanation: Some common verbs do not add -ed in the past. Learn their special past forms, and use the same word for every person.

practice.prompt: Ben arrived at the party early. Which verb fits?
practice.explanation: Came is the past form of come.

practice.prompt: Listen and choose what you heard.
practice.audio: My mother bought fruit at the supermarket.
practice.answer: My mother bought fruit at the supermarket.
options: My mother bought fruit at the supermarket.
My mother made soup in the kitchen.
My mother took a bus to the station.
practice.explanation: Bought is the past form of buy.

practice.prompt: Match each past verb to its base form.
practice.explanation: These four verbs change form in the past instead of adding -ed.

practice.prompt: Sam and Smarty baked a sweet dessert. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: They ___ a chocolate cake yesterday.
practice.explanation: Use made when someone prepares or creates something.

practice.prompt: Ana handed a present to Omar. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: Ana ___ Omar a blue pen.
practice.explanation: Ana is the person who handed the pen over, so use gave.

practice.prompt: Put the words in order.
practice.answer: He took the key from the table.
practice.explanation: Took is the past form of take.

practice.prompt: Zara went to see her aunt and got a nice scarf. Which two verbs fit?
practice.explanation: Visited means went to see, and got means received.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: I bought a sandwich and some juice.
practice.answer: I bought a sandwich and some juice.
practice.explanation: Bought is the past form of buy.

story.hook: What is inside the box Sam brought up to the old room?

image.describe: Sam and Smarty the black cat sit beside an open cardboard box in the attic with a handmade paper boat and a red scarf.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Hello, Sam! You came up here early.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Yes! I took this box from my bedroom.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: What is in it?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I made this small boat at school, and my aunt gave me this red scarf.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Look! I also got a hat from Mia, and she bought two apples for us.

questions.prompt: Who gave Sam the red scarf?
questions.explanation: Sam says: my aunt gave me this red scarf.

questions.prompt: What did Mia buy for Smarty and Sam?
questions.explanation: Smarty says: she bought two apples for us.

mission.setup: Smarty asks about things you bought, made, or got recently.

turns.smarty: Yesterday I bought a book. What did you buy or make?
turns.hint: Answer with 'I bought...' or 'I made...'

turns.smarty: Nice! What did a friend or parent give you?
turns.example: My friend gave me a pen.
turns.hint: Say 'My friend gave me...' or 'I got...'

lessons.title: More irregular verbs
lessons.scenario: Lily and Smarty sit on an old sofa in the attic and read an old notebook.

items.example: I found an old key under the sofa.
items.note: Use 'found' as the past form of 'find' when you discovered something.

items.example: We met our teacher at the library.
items.note: Say 'met' as the past form of 'meet' when people saw and greeted each other.

items.example: Lily wrote her name in the notebook.
items.note: Use 'wrote' as the past form of 'write' when someone put words on paper.

items.example: The dog ran fast in the park.
items.note: Say 'ran' as the past form of 'run' when someone moved quickly on foot.

items.example: My grandfather told us a good story.
items.note: Use 'told' as the past form of 'tell' when someone spoke to share information.

items.example: Smarty sat on the chair next to the window.
items.note: Say 'sat' as the past form of 'sit' when someone rested on a chair or the floor.

grammar.title: More irregular pairs
grammar.explanation: Many common verbs change their vowel in the past: find becomes found, write becomes wrote, run becomes ran, and sit becomes sat.
examples: I found a key in the box.

practice.prompt: Smarty looked under the table and saw his lost pencil. Which verb fits?
practice.explanation: Found is the past form of find.

practice.prompt: Listen and choose what you heard.
practice.audio: She wrote a postcard from England.
practice.answer: She wrote a postcard from England.
options: She wrote a postcard from England.
She found a map in England.
She met a friend in England.
practice.explanation: Wrote is the past form of write.

practice.prompt: Match each past verb to its base form.
practice.explanation: Each irregular past form matches one base verb.

practice.prompt: It started to rain, so Ben moved very fast to the bus. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: Ben ___ to the bus because it was raining.
practice.explanation: Ran is the past form of run.

practice.prompt: Smarty and Lily rested on the old sofa. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: They ___ on the sofa and read a book.
practice.explanation: Sat is the past form of sit.

practice.prompt: Put the words in order.
practice.explanation: Told is the past form of tell.

practice.prompt: Omar saw Zara at the station and handed her a ticket. Which two verbs fit?
practice.explanation: Met means saw and greeted, and gave means handed over.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: We found a blue notebook in the box.
practice.answer: We found a blue notebook in the box.
practice.explanation: Found is the past form of find.

story.hook: What did Lily find in the old notebook?

image.describe: Lily and Smarty the black cat sit together on an old floral sofa in the attic reading a small blue notebook.

lines.speaker: Lily
lines.text: Smarty, I found this blue notebook behind the lamp!

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Who wrote in it?

lines.speaker: Lily
lines.text: My grandmother! We sat here and she told me about it.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: What did she write?

lines.speaker: Lily
lines.text: She met my grandfather in the park, and their dog ran after a red ball!

questions.prompt: Where did Lily find the blue notebook?
questions.explanation: Lily says: I found this blue notebook behind the lamp.

questions.prompt: Where did Lily's grandmother meet her grandfather?
questions.explanation: Lily says: She met my grandfather in the park.

mission.setup: Smarty asks you to share a short note using irregular verbs from this lesson.

turns.smarty: Today I sat on the sofa and found a pen. Where did you sit or what did you find?
turns.hint: Start with 'I sat...' or 'I found...'

turns.smarty: And did you meet a friend or write something?
turns.hint: Say 'I met...' or 'I wrote...'

lessons.title: Review
lessons.scenario: Smarty quizzes Ben in the attic on regular and irregular past verbs.

practice.prompt: Match each regular past verb to its meaning.
practice.explanation: Regular past verbs end in -ed.

practice.prompt: Match each irregular past verb to its base verb.
practice.explanation: These four common verbs have irregular past forms.

practice.prompt: Ben carried bags for his grandmother on the way home. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: Ben ___ his grandmother and walked home.
practice.explanation: Helped means gave support to someone.

practice.prompt: Mia handed a book to Leo, so Leo received it. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: Mia ___ Leo a book, and he got happy.
practice.explanation: Gave is the past form of give.

practice.prompt: Listen and choose what you heard.
practice.audio: I found a pen and wrote a letter.
practice.answer: I found a pen and wrote a letter.
options: I found a pen and wrote a letter.
I bought a pen and made a cake.
I took a bus and met a friend.
practice.explanation: Found and wrote are the past forms of find and write.

practice.prompt: Zara saw Omar at the café and shared good news with him. Which two verbs fit?
practice.explanation: Met means saw and greeted; told means shared information.

practice.prompt: Put the words in order.
practice.explanation: Ran and sat are the past forms of run and sit.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: Yesterday we visited the museum and bought a postcard.
practice.answer: Yesterday we visited the museum and bought a postcard.
practice.explanation: Visited is regular (-ed) and bought is irregular.

story.hook: How did Ben spend his Saturday?

image.describe: Smarty the black cat sits on a wooden crate in the attic listening to Ben tell his weekend story.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Ben, tell me about your Saturday!

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: In the morning, I cleaned my room and helped my father.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: And in the afternoon?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: I walked to the park, met Omar, and we ran by the trees.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Did you have a good dinner?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Yes! My mother cooked pasta, and I wrote a postcard to my cousin.

questions.prompt: Who did Ben meet in the park?
questions.explanation: Ben says: I walked to the park, met Omar.

questions.prompt: What did Ben do after dinner?
questions.explanation: Ben says: I wrote a postcard to my cousin.

mission.setup: Tell Smarty two things you did on a past day using verbs from Lessons 1–3.

turns.smarty: Tell me one regular action you did: watched, cooked, visited, helped, cleaned, or walked.
turns.hint: Say 'I' plus one of the -ed verbs.

turns.smarty: Now tell me one irregular action: came, took, made, got, gave, bought, found, met, wrote, ran, told, or sat.
turns.hint: Say 'I' plus one of the irregular past verbs.

lessons.title: Did you?
lessons.canDo: Ask and answer about the past
lessons.scenario: Zara climbs up to the attic and asks Smarty and Leo about their weekend.

items.example: Did they go to the cinema yesterday?
items.note: Start a past yes/no question with 'Did' followed by the person and the base verb.

items.example: I did not watch TV last night.
items.note: Use 'did not' plus the base verb to say something did not happen.

items.example: Did you clean your room? Yes, I did.
items.note: Use 'Yes, I did' as a short, natural answer when the answer is yes.

items.example: Did you buy bread? No, I did not.
items.note: Use 'No, I did not' as a short answer when you did not do something.

items.example: You had an exam yesterday. How did it go?
items.note: Ask 'How did it go?' to find out if an event or test went well or badly.

items.example: Where did you go last weekend?
items.note: Ask 'Where did you go?' when you want to know the place someone visited.

grammar.title: Questions and negatives with did
grammar.explanation: After did or did not, always use the base verb (go, watch, buy), not the past form. Short answers use Yes, I did or No, I did not.

practice.prompt: You want to ask if Sam and Mia went to the park. Choose the right question.
practice.answer: Did they go to the park?
options: Did they go to the park?
Did they went to the park?
Do they went to the park?
practice.explanation: Use Did + subject + base verb (go).

practice.prompt: Leo stayed home and skipped TV last night. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: I ___ watch TV last night.
practice.explanation: Use did not before the base verb for past negatives.

practice.prompt: Match each question to the best answer.
practice.explanation: Match yes/no questions with Yes, I did / No, I did not, and Wh- questions with details.

practice.prompt: Listen and choose what you heard.
practice.audio: Where did you go on Sunday?
practice.answer: Where did you go on Sunday?
options: Where did you go on Sunday?
How did it go on Sunday?
practice.explanation: Where asks about a place.

practice.prompt: Leo had a maths test. Ask him about it.
practice.explanation: Use the base verb go after did.

practice.prompt: Smarty asks: Did you cook dinner? You ate a cold sandwich instead. Complete your answer.
practice.text: ___, I did not.
practice.explanation: Say No, I did not when you did not do the action.

practice.prompt: Say the question aloud.
practice.text: Where did you go last weekend?
practice.answer: Where did you go last weekend?
practice.explanation: Use Where did you go to ask about a past trip or outing.

story.hook: How did Leo's history exam go?

image.describe: Zara climbs the wooden attic stairs to chat with Smarty the black cat and Leo, who holds a graded history paper.

lines.speaker: Zara
lines.text: Hi, Leo! You had a history exam yesterday. How did it go?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: It went well! I passed!

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Well done, Leo! Where did you go after school?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: I went to the café with Sam and Mia.

lines.speaker: Zara
lines.text: Did they go to the cinema too?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: No, they did not. I did not go either, because I was tired.

lines.speaker: Zara
lines.text: Did you sleep early?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Yes, I did!

questions.prompt: Where did Leo go after school?
questions.explanation: Leo says: I went to the café with Sam and Mia.

questions.prompt: Did Sam and Mia go to the cinema?
questions.explanation: Leo says: No, they did not.

mission.setup: Smarty asks you about your last weekend. Answer with Yes, I did, No, I did not, or where you went.

turns.smarty: Where did you go last weekend?
turns.hint: Answer with 'I went to...'

turns.smarty: Did you watch TV yesterday?
turns.hint: Say 'Yes, I did' or 'No, I did not'.

lessons.title: Time words
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Omar look at old calendars and boxes in the attic to see when things happened.

items.example: I drank tea and ate bread this morning.
items.note: Use 'this morning' for the early part of today.

items.example: We had three exams last week.
items.note: Say 'last week' for the seven days before this week.

items.example: They visited England last year.
items.note: Use 'last year' for the calendar year before this year.

items.example: My grandfather made this chair a long time ago.
items.note: Say 'a long time ago' when something happened many years in the past.

items.example: I met my best friend five years ago.
items.note: Put 'years ago' after a number to say how many years back something happened.

items.example: When I was little, I loved sweet apples.
items.note: Start or end a sentence with 'when I was little' to talk about your childhood.

grammar.title: Past time expressions
grammar.explanation: Place time phrases at the start or end of a past sentence. Put ago after a number of years, months, or days.
examples: We visited Brazil two years ago.
When I was little, I had a small cat.

practice.prompt: Omar ate breakfast at eight o'clock today. Which time phrase fits?
practice.explanation: This morning refers to the morning of today.

practice.prompt: Match each time expression to what it describes.
practice.explanation: These time phrases move from recent past to distant past.

practice.prompt: Mia moved to this house three years in the past. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: Mia came here three ___.
practice.explanation: Use years ago right after a number like three.

practice.prompt: Listen and choose what you heard.
practice.audio: When I was little, I had a small dog.
practice.answer: When I was little, I had a small dog.
options: When I was little, I had a small dog.
Last year, I bought a small dog.
This morning, I walked my small dog.
practice.explanation: When I was little talks about early childhood.

practice.prompt: Put the words in order.
practice.answer: He wrote this book a long time ago.
practice.explanation: A long time ago goes at the end of the sentence.

practice.prompt: We visited the museum seven days ago. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: We visited the museum ___.
practice.explanation: Last week means the week before this one.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: I visited Uzbekistan last year.
practice.explanation: Last year places the trip in the previous year.

story.hook: How old is the wooden clock Omar found in the old room?

image.describe: Smarty the black cat and Omar examine an antique wooden clock and an old map on a table in the attic.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Smarty, look at this clock! When did your family get it?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: My grandfather bought it a long time ago.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Did it work last year?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Yes! It worked ten years ago, and it worked last week too.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: What happened? Did it stop this morning?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: No, I cleaned it when I was little, and it still ticks!

questions.prompt: When did Smarty's grandfather buy the clock?
questions.explanation: Smarty says: My grandfather bought it a long time ago.

questions.prompt: When did Smarty clean the clock?
questions.explanation: Smarty says: I cleaned it when I was little.

mission.setup: Smarty asks when you did different things. Use time phrases from this lesson.

turns.smarty: This morning I had milk. What did you do this morning?
turns.hint: Include 'this morning' in your answer.

turns.smarty: What did you like when you were little?
turns.example: When I was little, I loved cake.
turns.hint: Start with 'When I was little, I liked...' or 'When I was little, I had...'

lessons.title: Old things
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Ana open a wooden chest in the attic full of old keepsakes.

items.example: I found an old photo of my parents.
items.note: Say 'old photo' for a picture taken with a camera in the past.

image.describe: a faded sepia photograph of two smiling kittens sitting on a garden bench

items.example: This small red car was my favourite toy.
items.note: A 'toy' is an object that children play with.

image.describe: a small painted wooden toy train resting on an attic rug

items.example: Ana wrote about her day in her diary.
items.note: A 'diary' is a private notebook where you write what happened each day.

image.describe: a small blue notebook diary with a tiny brass lock and a ribbon bookmark

items.example: We found a box of treasure in the old room.
items.note: Use 'treasure' for special or valuable things kept safe in a box.

image.describe: an open wooden chest glowing with shiny gold coins, shells, and colorful stones

items.example: That summer picnic is a happy memory.
items.note: A 'memory' is something from the past that you remember in your mind.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat smiling warmly with a thought cloud showing a sunny picnic

items.example: My grandmother kept every old photo in an album.
items.note: An 'album' is a special book where you put photos.

image.describe: an open leather-bound photo album showing neat pages of family cat snapshots

practice.prompt: Look at the picture from a camera taken years ago. What is it?
practice.explanation: An old photo is a picture from the past.

practice.prompt: Match each word to its description.

pairs.right: a book where you write about your day

practice.explanation: Each keepsake has a clear purpose.

practice.prompt: Listen and choose what you heard.
practice.audio: She wrote in her diary every night.
practice.answer: She wrote in her diary every night.
options: She wrote in her diary every night.
She sat with her toy every night.
She cleaned her album every night.
practice.explanation: A diary is where you write daily notes.

practice.prompt: Ana thinks about her birthday party last year and smiles. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: Her birthday party is a happy ___.
practice.explanation: A memory is something nice or important you remember from the past.

practice.prompt: We put twenty family pictures inside a big book. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: The old photos are in the ___.
practice.explanation: An album holds photos.

practice.prompt: Put the words in order.
practice.answer: We found a box of treasure.
practice.explanation: Treasure means special or valuable things.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: When I was little, I had a small toy train.
practice.answer: When I was little, I had a small toy train.
practice.explanation: Toy describes a plaything from childhood.

story.hook: What treasure does Ana find inside the wooden box?

image.describe: Ana and Smarty the black cat kneel beside an open wooden chest in the attic holding a photo album, a small diary, and a toy boat.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Smarty, this box is full of treasure!

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Look at that green album. There is an old photo on the first page.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: That is my father when he was little! He had a small toy boat.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: And here is a red diary under the album.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: He wrote about that boat in his diary. What a good memory!

questions.prompt: What is on the first page of the green album?
questions.explanation: Smarty says: There is an old photo on the first page.

questions.prompt: Where did Ana's father write about his toy boat?
questions.explanation: Ana says: He wrote about that boat in his diary.

mission.setup: Smarty asks you about old keepsakes and happy memories.

turns.smarty: I have an old photo in my album. Do you have an old photo, a toy, or a diary?
turns.hint: Say 'I have an old photo', 'I have a toy', or 'I have a diary'.

turns.smarty: Tell me one happy memory from last year or when you were little.
turns.hint: Start with 'Last year I...' or 'When I was little, I...'

lessons.title: Review
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Mia sort old photos in the attic and test each other on questions, time words, and keepsakes.

practice.prompt: Match each past question or negative to its meaning.
practice.explanation: Use did in past questions and did not in past negatives.

practice.prompt: Mia asks: Did you find your diary? You found it in your bag. Complete the reply.
practice.explanation: Use Yes, I did for a positive short answer.

practice.prompt: Smarty asks: Did you buy a new toy? You did not buy one. Complete the reply.
practice.text: ___, I did not.
practice.explanation: Use No, I did not for a negative short answer.

practice.prompt: Match each time expression to an example.

pairs.right: at eight o'clock in the morning

practice.explanation: Time words place past events clearly in time.

practice.prompt: Listen and choose what you heard.
practice.audio: When I was little, I found an old photo in an album.
practice.answer: When I was little, I found an old photo in an album.
options: When I was little, I found an old photo in an album.
This morning, I found a toy in my diary.
Last year, we found treasure in the park.
practice.explanation: An album holds old photos from childhood.

practice.prompt: This small box of coins is special to Sam because it brings back a happy ___. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: A memory is something from the past you remember warmly.

practice.prompt: Put the words in order.
practice.answer: She wrote this diary ten years ago.
practice.explanation: Put ten years ago at the end of the sentence.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: Where did you go last week?
practice.answer: Where did you go last week?

story.hook: What did Mia find in the old album?

image.describe: Mia and Smarty the black cat sit at a table in the attic looking through an open photo album with old photos.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Mia, you came up here this morning. Where did you go after lunch?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: I visited my grandmother, and she gave me this album.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: How did it go? Did you find good photos?

lines.speaker: Mia

lines.text: You were little! And that small cat next to you is me!

lines.speaker: Mia

questions.prompt: How old is the photo Mia showed Smarty?
questions.explanation: Mia says: Look at this old photo from eight years ago.

questions.prompt: Did Mia forget that day?
questions.explanation: Mia says: I did not forget that day.

mission.setup: Smarty tests your memory with two quick questions about the past.

lessons.title: Childhood
lessons.scenario: Looking through the old album in the attic, Smarty and Tom talk about when they were little.

items.example: I met my best friend in kindergarten.
items.note: ‘Kindergarten’ is the school for young children before primary school.

image.describe: a cheerful classroom for young kittens with low tables, colorful blocks, and crayon drawings

items.example: After school, we ran to the playground.
items.note: A ‘playground’ is an outdoor area with games and equipment for children.

image.describe: a sunny outdoor playground with a yellow slide, climbing bars, and soft green grass

items.example: Lily slept with her brown teddy bear.
items.note: A ‘teddy bear’ is a soft toy bear that children love to hug.

image.describe: a cuddly brown plush teddy bear wearing a red ribbon sitting on a bed

items.example: Tom got his first blue bicycle when he was six.
items.note: A ‘bicycle’ is a two-wheeled vehicle that you ride with pedals.

image.describe: a small blue children's bicycle with a shiny bell and a wicker basket

items.example: My grandmother always gave us fruit sweets.
items.note: ‘Sweets’ are small sugary treats like candies.

image.describe: a clear glass jar filled with colorful wrapped fruit sweets and candies

items.example: Mia sat on the swing and went high.
items.note: A ‘swing’ is a hanging seat in a park or garden that moves back and forth.

image.describe: a wooden swing hanging by sturdy ropes from a big leafy garden tree

practice.prompt: Tom was four years old and went to school for young children. Where did he go?

lessons.title: Big events
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Lily find a trophy and a map in the attic and share stories about big events.

items.example: Ben had a small accident on his bicycle, but he was fine.
items.note: An ‘accident’ is something bad that happens by mistake, like falling off a bike.

image.describe: a kitten sitting on the grass next to a fallen bicycle with a spilled basket of apples

items.example: A big storm came with heavy rain and wind.
items.note: A ‘storm’ is very bad weather with strong wind and heavy rain.

image.describe: dark storm clouds with wind and heavy rain bending trees outside an attic window

items.example: My friends made a birthday surprise for me.
items.note: A ‘surprise’ is something nice or unexpected that you did not know about.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat smiling in amazement as friends pop out with a birthday cake

items.example: Our trip to the mountains was a great adventure.
items.note: An ‘adventure’ is an exciting, unusual experience or trip.

image.describe: two explorer cats wearing backpacks and holding a map on a sunny forest hill

items.example: The train journey to Uzbekistan took ten hours.
items.note: A ‘journey’ is the act of travelling from one place to another.

image.describe: a red passenger train travelling along tracks across green hills toward distant peaks

items.example: Lily got first prize in the art test.
items.note: A ‘prize’ is something you win in a game, race, or competition.

image.describe: a shiny gold star medal with a blue ribbon held proudly by a smiling kitten

practice.prompt: The sky went dark, and strong wind and heavy rain began. What was it?
practice.explanation: A storm brings strong wind and heavy rain.

practice.prompt: Match each event word to its meaning.

pairs.right: you get it when you are good

practice.prompt: Listen and choose what you heard.

We had a small accident at school.

practice.explanation: A journey is travel from one place to another.

practice.prompt: Put the words in order.
practice.answer: The birthday cake was a nice surprise.
practice.explanation: Surprise means an unexpected happy gift or event.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: He had a small accident on his bicycle.
practice.answer: He had a small accident on his bicycle.
practice.explanation: Accident is used for an unplanned fall or crash.

story.hook: How did Lily get the gold prize in the old room?

lines.text: Lily, where did you get that gold prize?

lines.text: I got it last year! It was a big adventure.

lines.text: Tell me about it!

lessons.title: Tell a story
lessons.scenario: Smarty shows Sam how to tell a past story step by step in the attic.

items.example: At first, the weather was sunny and warm.
items.note: Start a story with 'At first' to show how things were in the beginning.

items.example: We ate lunch, and afterwards we walked to the park.
items.note: Use 'afterwards' to show what happened after an earlier event.

items.example: First we cleaned the table, and next we made tea.
items.note: Say 'next' to introduce the following step in your story.

items.example: We were in the garden, and suddenly a storm came.
items.note: Use 'suddenly' when something happens fast and by surprise.

items.example: We looked everywhere, and finally we found the key.
items.note: Say 'finally' to introduce the last event at the end of a story.

items.example: The train was late, but at last we came home.
items.note: Use 'at last' when something good happens after a long wait.

grammar.title: Order words in a story
grammar.explanation: Link past events clearly: use at first for the start, next and afterwards for later steps, suddenly for a fast surprise, and finally or at last for the ending.
examples: At first it was sunny, and suddenly it rained.
At last we found our home.

practice.prompt: You want to describe how the day began before anything changed. Which phrase fits?
practice.explanation: At first shows the beginning of a situation.

practice.prompt: Match each story word to its role.
practice.explanation: These linking words give your story a clear order.

practice.prompt: They were walking quietly when a big dog jumped out fast. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: We walked in the park, and ___ a dog ran to us.
practice.explanation: Suddenly shows a quick, surprising action.

practice.prompt: Listen and choose what you heard.
practice.audio: We visited the museum, and afterwards we had lunch.
practice.answer: We visited the museum, and afterwards we had lunch.
options: We visited the museum, and afterwards we had lunch.
At first we visited the library, and next we went home.
Finally we walked to the station in the rain.
practice.explanation: Afterwards shows what happened next in time.

practice.prompt: After waiting two hours at the station, the train arrived. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: We waited for two hours, and ___ the train came.
practice.explanation: At last shows relief after waiting a long time.

practice.prompt: Put the words in order.
practice.answer: Next we cooked soup, and finally we ate.
practice.explanation: Use next for the middle step and finally for the ending.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: At first it was cloudy, and suddenly a storm came.
practice.answer: At first it was cloudy, and suddenly a storm came.
practice.explanation: At first sets the scene, and suddenly introduces the storm.

story.hook: How did Sam and Smarty find the missing key in the old room?

image.describe: Sam and Smarty the black cat search around dusty boxes in the attic until Smarty spots a shiny brass key under a rug.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Sam, tell me how you found the key yesterday!

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: At first, I looked on the table, but it was not there.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: What did you do next?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Next, I cleaned behind the big box, and afterwards I sat on the chair.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: And then?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Suddenly, you jumped under the chair, and finally we found the key! At last!

questions.prompt: Where did Sam look at first?

questions.prompt: How did they find the key at last?
questions.explanation: Sam says: Suddenly, you jumped under the chair, and finally we found the key.

lessons.title: A day I remember
lessons.scenario: Smarty and his friends gather in the attic for a final memory challenge.

items.example: I remember when we had a picnic by the lake.
items.note: Start a story with 'I remember when' to share a clear memory from the past.

items.text: It was a long time ago
items.example: It was a long time ago, when I was in kindergarten.
items.note: Say 'It was a long time ago' to show your story happened many years back.

items.example: You found an old box! What happened next?
items.note: Ask 'What happened next?' when you want to hear the rest of someone's story.

practice.prompt: You want to share a happy memory from childhood. How can you start?
practice.answer: I remember when I got my first bicycle.
options: I remember when I got my first bicycle.
practice.explanation: I remember when introduces a past memory.

practice.prompt: Listen and choose what you heard.
practice.audio: It was a long time ago, when I was little.
practice.answer: It was a long time ago, when I was little.
options: It was a long time ago, when I was little.
It was this morning, at breakfast.
It was last week, at the supermarket.
practice.explanation: It was a long time ago places the memory far in the past.

practice.prompt: Your friend stops in the middle of a story. Ask them to continue.
practice.explanation: What happened next? asks for the next event in a story.

practice.prompt: Match each past verb to its base form.
practice.explanation: These irregular verbs are key for telling past stories.

practice.prompt: Zara asked if Leo went to the park, and he answered no. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: No, I ___ go to the park.
practice.explanation: Use did not + base verb for past negatives.

practice.prompt: The sky was clear, and then without warning the rain began. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: At first it was sunny, and ___ a storm came.
practice.explanation: Suddenly marks a fast, unexpected change.

practice.prompt: Mia opened her ___ and looked at an ___ from kindergarten. Which words fit?
practice.explanation: An album holds old photos from childhood.

practice.prompt: After a long walk in the mountains, they arrived at their hotel. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: We walked for four hours, and ___ we arrived at the hotel.
practice.explanation: Finally introduces the end of a sequence of events.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: I remember when we visited our grandmother five years ago.
practice.answer: I remember when we visited our grandmother five years ago.
practice.explanation: Combines I remember when, a past verb, and years ago.
